gaps: Rohdaten Export, Linienanalyse DPM and Datenqualitätsindex DPM evaluations have no report view at all (state map not_exercised), so how those three of five evaluation types are read cannot be assessed this round — the missing 'Anzeigen' on their list rows was already raised as round 1 UX-3/CLR-1 and is not re-reported here.

findings.element: Pünktlichkeit report (view-report-punct) — 'Break down by / Aufschlüsseln' selects #punct-auf-1 / #punct-auf-2 / #punct-auf-3
findings.finding: The punctuality report's three breakdown selects half-work: the cascade disables already-used levels so the control feels alive, but the table is re-rendered from the same bundle data and never regroups, and the change produces no message either.
findings.user_impact: The analyst's core question — 'show me this by stop / by TU / by month' — silently returns the line-bundle view every time, so they either read the wrong grouping as if it were the one they asked for or conclude the report is broken and stop.
findings.suggested_fix: Make renderPunctReport() read #punct-auf-1/-2/-3 and regroup (and relabel the first column) accordingly, or disable the selects and state that only the line-bundle grouping is available.

evidence.action: Logged in, opened 'Pünktlichkeit – Letzter Monat, Kanton ZH' via Anzeigen, then set level 1 to Haltestelle, then level 1 = TU konzessioniert + level 2 = Monat (real Chromium, 1440×1000).
evidence.observed: Row count stayed 26, first column header stayed 'Name / Line bundle', first data row stayed 'AAGL BusÜ 1' in all three states, and no snackbar or loading state appeared. Source confirms it: punctCascade() only toggles option.disabled then calls renderPunctReport(), which iterates PUNCT_DATA.bundles and never reads the three select values (index.html:7060–7126). Distinct from AUTO-6, which is the V5 report's #rpt-aufschluss-* selects; these three do have onchange handlers.

findings.element: Pünktlichkeit report — bundle row expander caret (.punct-expand-btn) on every line-bundle row
findings.finding: The expander needs two clicks to open, because the button ships without .collapsed while the line rows ship hidden, so the first click re-hides rows that are already hidden — and the caret icon is 'expand_more' in both states, so nothing on screen shows which state the row is in.
findings.user_impact: Drilling from a bundle into its individual lines appears not to work, so the analyst gives up on the drill-down (or, after the first successful open, cannot tell which rows are expanded and loses their place in a 26-row table).
findings.suggested_fix: Give the button the .collapsed class in the initial render and swap the icon to expand_less when the row is open.

evidence.action: From a fresh load of view-report-punct, clicked the first bundle caret three times and measured visible #punct-tbody rows and the button's icon plus .collapsed class after each click.
evidence.observed: 20 visible rows / 'expand_more', collapsed=false → click 1: 20 rows (no change) / 'expand_more', collapsed=true → click 2: 26 rows / 'expand_more', collapsed=false. The icon text never changed. Matches togglePunctBundle() at index.html:7105–7113, which reads .collapsed before toggling it.

findings.element: Pünktlichkeit report — header and summary band (no .page-subtitle, no KPI card region), compared with its two sibling reports
findings.finding: The punctuality report opens with no summary figures at all — no KPI cards, no threshold marker and no generated-at line — while the two other report types lead with exactly that, so the same product answers 'how did we do' three different ways.
findings.user_impact: An analyst who opens the punctuality report to read the headline number has to find and interpret the 'Gesamt' row of a 26-row table instead, and gets no threshold comparison and no indication of when the figures were produced.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the punctuality report the same KPI band its siblings have (overall Wert % against its threshold, plus the period and generation time in the header).

evidence.action: Opened all three report views in turn through their real Anzeigen buttons and counted KPI/card elements and .page-subtitle in each.
evidence.observed: view-report-connection: 4 .rpt-kpi-card cards ('ALL DAY 89,53% ⚠ Threshold: 90%' …). view-report-fa: 3 .fa-kpi-card cards (Trips 953'278 / 33'483 Cancelled …). view-report-punct: 0 card elements of any kind. .page-subtitle is null on all three and no 'generated / as of' text appears in any of them.

findings.element: Parameters bar of the report views — expandable chips "37 TU's ▾" and "17 Kantone ▾" (.rpt-param-chip--partial + .rpt-chip-dropdown)
findings.finding: Two of the parameter chips carry a dropdown caret and a pointer cursor, so they read as the report's filters, but they expand into a read-only list with no checkboxes, no Apply and no way to change what the report covers.
findings.user_impact: An analyst who wants to narrow a 37-TU report to one operator clicks the chip that looks built for exactly that, scrolls a list of abbreviations, finds nothing selectable and has no signal that the only route is to create a new evaluation.
findings.suggested_fix: Present these as read-only scope information — drop the pointer cursor/caret in favour of a plain 'show all' disclosure, and put an explicit 'Change parameters' action next to them that reopens the evaluation setup.

evidence.action: Clicked the '37 TU's ▾' chip in view-report-punct, inspected the panel contents and the computed cursor on the chip and on its items, and clicked the chip a second time.
evidence.observed: Panel opens with a header and 37 plain .rpt-chip-dd-item divs (AAGL, AAGR, AAGS …), no input or onclick on any item, no Apply/Cancel anywhere in the panel; a second click collapses it. Computed cursor is 'pointer' on the chip but 'auto' on the items, i.e. the container invites a click the contents cannot honour.

findings.element: Evaluations list (view-reports-list) — rows with the red 'Failed' status badge (4 of 28 rows)
findings.finding: A failed evaluation is a dead end: the red badge gives no reason, carries no tooltip and is not clickable, and the row's only action is delete — there is no retry and no route to the error.
findings.user_impact: The analyst who came to read a report is told it failed but not why or what to do, so the only move the UI offers is to destroy the evidence and rebuild the whole evaluation from scratch, without knowing whether it will fail again the same way.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the Failed badge open a short reason ('no data for the selected period', 'import incomplete') and add a 'Retry' action alongside delete.

evidence.action: Inspected all four Failed rows in the logged-in list (status cell markup, title attributes, onclick on the row and on the status cell, action-column contents) and clicked a Failed status cell.
evidence.observed: Status cell is …Failed with no title attribute; row onclick and status-cell onclick are both null; the actions column contains a single button, title="Delete", onclick="deleteEvaluation(this)". Clicking the badge changed nothing (page text length identical before and after).
